correctness.rationale: All equilibria solved exactly by stationary per-capita difference and sum. Symmetric Jacobian gives exact eigenvalue crossing at a=3/4, and explicit off-diagonal determinant is positive only in 3/4<a<1. Scalar upper and eventual lower logistic bounds rule out boundary omega limits, Bendixson-Dulac 1/(xy) gives strict divergence -(1/x+1/y), and the only interior saddle has global stable manifold the diagonal. Local center manifold at a=3/4 has s=2/3-3d²/8+O(d⁴), d_dot=-3d³/8+O(d⁵), giving the verified t-constants. The bundled exact symbolic checker passed; it is supplemental not the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2024 primary article provides broad structural conditions, not the sharp exact one-parameter basin/critical-amplitude theorem. Vet et al. 2018 already show interior bistability in more general models including mutualism: generic coexistence bistability is expressly excluded from novelty. Novelty judged on the exact pure-competition interval, all-positive-initial-data basin partition, and nonhyperbolic slowing, not the general phenomenon. Other closest records involve dissimilar objects. Same mathematical model literature assessment only; residual risk of unindexed equivalent normal form remains.
residual_risks: The 2018 extended-LV model is a genuine higher-dimensional parameter superset of the polynomial ODE and already describes two stable positive coexistence points; generic existence is not original and is explicitly excluded.
An older unindexed exact symmetric polynomial-bifurcation example, a comprehensive ecology monograph or a generic theorem could imply this precise result.

value.rationale: Pure cross-quadratic competition with normalized self-logistic growth is the smallest natural exchange-symmetric cubic density normal form; one coefficient a sets the two ecological regimes. It is not an arbitrary finite numerical slice: the threshold, complete basin separator and exact t^{-1/2} imbalance law are structurally meaningful and the coexistence states remain mutually invadable. Motivated by the ecological misuse of mutual invasion as a unique outcome predictor. No general theorem about arbitrary asymmetric high-order ecological networks is asserted.
